drug_name: Zinc Oxide, Niacinamide, Colloidal Sulfur, Azelaic Acid, Salicylic Acid (Combination Topical)
brand_names: Varies by compounded or commercial formulation
May be dispensed as a custom compounded product
what_its_for: This combination skin treatment is used to help control acne, reduce redness, calm irritated skin, and improve the overall look and feel of your skin. Each ingredient works together: zinc oxide and niacinamide soothe and protect the skin, colloidal sulfur and azelaic acid fight acne-causing bacteria and reduce inflammation, and salicylic acid unclogs pores by gently removing dead skin cells.
how_to_take: This medicine is applied directly to your skin (topical use only — do NOT swallow). Start by washing your face or affected area gently with a mild cleanser and patting it dry. Apply a thin, even layer of the product to the affected areas as directed by your doctor or pharmacist. Wash your hands thoroughly before and after applying. Avoid getting the product in your eyes, mouth, nose, or on broken or irritated skin. If accidental eye contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with cool water.
dosing: Use this product exactly as your doctor or pharmacist has instructed. A common routine is to apply it once or twice daily (morning and/or evening). Start with a small amount to see how your skin reacts. Do not apply more than directed, as using too much can increase skin dryness or irritation without giving you better results.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled application. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular routine. Do not apply a double dose to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store this product at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C–25°C), unless your pharmacist has given you different instructions. Keep it away from direct sunlight, heat, and moisture. Keep the lid tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children and pets. If the product was compounded by a pharmacy, check your label for specific expiration and storage instructions, and do not use it after the expiration date.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using other strong acne products (like benzoyl peroxide, retinoids, or other exfoliants) on the same area at the same time unless your doctor approves, as this can cause excessive dryness, peeling, or irritation. Avoid prolonged sun exposure while using this product — always apply a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher sunscreen during the day, since salicylic acid and azelaic acid can make your skin more sensitive to the sun. Avoid tanning beds. Do not use on sunburned, windburned, or very dry and broken skin. Avoid waxing treated areas, as skin may be more sensitive.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or pharmacist if you experience: severe skin redness, burning, or peeling that does not improve; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; unusual skin discoloration (lighter or darker patches) that was not there before; worsening of your acne after several weeks of use; or any other unexpected skin changes that concern you.
when_it_works: Skin treatments like this one take time to work. Most people begin to notice some improvement in their skin within 4 to 6 weeks of regular use. The best results are typically seen after 8 to 12 weeks of consistent daily use. Do not get discouraged if you do not see immediate results — be patient and stick to your routine. If you see no improvement after 12 weeks, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this product if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Azelaic acid and niacinamide are generally considered safer options during pregnancy, but always check with your healthcare provider first. Children: This product should only be used in children under the supervision of a healthcare provider. Elderly: Elderly patients may have more sensitive or dry skin — start with less frequent application and monitor for irritation. Sensitive skin: If you have very sensitive skin or a history of eczema or rosacea, let your doctor know before starting this treatment.
